## In development
The curriculum is planned, not a completed course. Available now: unit previews,
readiness guidance, project outlines, and an executable offline smoke lab.
**0 of 101 lessons and 0 of 25 unit challenges are released.**
:::

## Build systems you can explain and defend

For learners with **project-ready Python**, this course moves from deterministic
agent fixtures to bounded runtimes, tools, retrieval, memory, protocols, evaluation,
safety, durable services, and production decisions. Start with a non-agentic baseline;
add autonomy only when evidence justifies it.

[Check your readiness](readiness.qmd) · [Run the smoke lab](../../resources/agent-lab.qmd)

## Planned scope and pacing

- **25 units:** Unit 0 has five lessons; Units 1–24 have four each.
- **101 lessons and 25 challenges**, with three short checkpoints per substantial lesson.
- **Four numbered milestone projects**, plus architecture and advanced checkpoints.
- **One capstone**, developed through six stages.
- **Draft effort:** 240–360 hours plus optional extensions. Activity estimates,
  milestone overlap, and the 40–70 hour capstone need calibration during authoring;
  this is not a validated total workload.
- Adding the current activity ranges without overlap deductions gives roughly
  261–462 hours before cumulative reviews. This arithmetic is a reconciliation
  warning, not a new validated estimate; learner pilots must resolve the range
  and pacing before release.
- Standard: 30–36 weeks at 7–10 hours/week; intensive: 18–22 weeks at 12–16 hours/week;
  extended: 9–12 months. Adjust to actual lab time, not reading speed.

## Learn from observable evidence

**Specify → Predict → Run → Inspect → Explain → Modify → Evaluate → Attack → Record.**
Use deterministic fixtures first. Inspect actions, state, tool results, traces,
metrics, and concise external rationales—not private chain-of-thought. Network
experiments will have fixture fallbacks; paid providers are never needed for core work.

Planned case studies include OpenClaw for persistent-assistant architecture and
operations, and Hermes Agent for memory and reusable procedures. Learn the
mechanisms through course fixtures first; live integrations are optional after
the safety prerequisites, not required accounts or validated labs today. New
tools must earn adoption through the same baselines, tests, and permission
boundaries as the framework-free implementation.
